subject: Geo-ownership & log custody: quick recap and next steps
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Anna Klein <anna.klein@medsourcehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Geo-ownership & log custody: quick recap and next steps

Hi Anna — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick written recap so we have the items captured and a clear set of next steps from our side.

Summary of what we covered:
- PII handling: Redwood does not use customer content to train shared models. We treat customer inputs/outputs as customer-owned.
- Retention: default runtime logs retained for 90 days; request-level artefacts (full payloads) can be configured by customer with retention controls.
- Audit/logging: all request metadata and admin-audit trails are captured and can be exported; logs are searchable in Console or via S3 export.
- Region pinning: customers can request region pins (US, EU, APAC). Pinning guarantees primary data residency; cross-region failover is permitted under a configured DR policy.
- Backups & snapshots: cold backups for model state and operational snapshots are stored in the pinned region by default; we support encrypted cross-region replication if required by policy.

Open questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Whether MedSource requires keys to be customer-managed (KMS/HSM) for at-rest encryption.
2) Maximum acceptable log retention window for audit evidence (you mentioned 12+ months as a possibility).
3) Failover direction rules — do you allow EU->US failover during incidents or prefer EU-only fallback?
4) Any additional export/ingest controls for PII (e.g., redaction before storage).

Attachments: redwood-geo-technical-summary.pdf (high level architecture + behavior matrix).

Suggested next steps:
- We propose a 30-minute technical deep-dive with MedSource Security to walk through KMS options, retention SLAs, and a sample data flow diagram. Ben and Laura will join to map contractual controls.
- If you can share a short questionnaire or a sample requirement sheet we’ll mark up the MAP (mutual action plan) and return a redline within 48 hours.

Would 10:00–11:00 PT on Thursday work for a technical call? If not, propose two alternatives and we’ll adapt.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | (415) 555-0197
Redwood Inference

From: Anna Klein <anna.klein@medsourcehealth.com>

Cc: MedSource Security <security@medsourcehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo-ownership & log custody: quick recap and next steps

Connor — thanks for the clear recap. A couple clarifications from our side before the tech call: 

> 1) KMS/HSM requirement
Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys for data at rest (we need customer key control for some datasets)? If yes, is HSM-backed KMS an option for Dedicated/Private customers?

> 2) Retention
You mentioned 90 days default for runtime logs. For compliance we may need 13 months of immutable audit logs for admin access events. Do you offer write-once or append-only options for audit trails, and can we export preserved copies monthly?

> 3) Failover behavior
If our primary region is EU, during a regional incident are you able to fail traffic to a US cold standby? If yes, what are the controls around data residency notifications and duration limits for cross-region processing?

> 4) Data flow diagram
Please include a simple data flow diagram that shows where PII lands, what is cached vs persisted, and which systems have access to cleartext.

We'd like to include those items on the tech call agenda. Also please send your SOC2 Type II report and any standard encryption whitepaper beforehand.

Thanks,
Anna Klein
Head of Security Programs, MedSource Health
anna.klein@medsourcehealth.com

--

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Geo-ownership & log custody: quick recap and next steps

Connor / Laura — draft replies and proposed plan below (for Connor to send to Anna):

Draft answers to Anna's numbered items:
1) KMS/HSM: Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted customers we provide envelope encryption with customer KMS integration (bring-your-own-KMS supported for enterprise tier). HSM-backed key custody is available on Private (on-prem) and via supported partners for Dedicated. (Action: Laura to confirm partner names and SOC/HSM attestation.)

2) Retention: Default runtime request logs 90 days. We can enable 13-month immutable audit retention for admin/audit events with monthly export snapshots to your S3 bucket (immutable via object lock). We need to confirm exact event types you need retained (admin access, model inference request metadata, redaction metadata). (Action: Connor to ask which event types are required.)

3) Failover: We can configure cross-region failover (EU->US) under a documented DR policy. During failover we can mark requests as "processing_in_non_primary_region" and emit an event; duration limits and notification hooks are configurable. If strict residency is required, we can implement a regional-only failover policy (no cross-region processing).

4) Data flow diagram: attached a quick draft map to iterate on: draft-map-of-data-flows.png. Add notes for redaction points and where KV caches are ephemeral.

Next steps recommended:
- Send SOC2 Type II and encryption whitepaper now (I'll pull the latest PDF).
- Book the 30-minute tech session — propose Thu 10:00 PT or Fri 08:00 PT.
- Ask Anna to specify which admin/audit event classes are in scope for the 13-month retention.

I'll let you two finalize and ship.

-Ben

Subject: Re: Geo-ownership & log custody: quick recap and next steps

Anna — thanks, and great questions. Responses inline below, plus links and proposed times.

> KMS/HSM requirement
- Yes: we support customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated and Private customers. For our Hosted offering we support BYOK (bring-your-own-key) integration with major cloud KMS providers; keys are never persisted in plaintext within Redwood. HSM-backed key custody is available for Private/on-prem; for Dedicated we can integrate with partner HSM providers (we'll confirm vendor attestation).

> Retention (13 months)
- We can enable 13-month immutable retention for admin/audit events. Implementation details: enable object-lock on an export S3 bucket and schedule monthly snapshots of audit tables. Event classes we typically include: admin sign-ins, role changes, API token creation/deletion, and admin-triggered data exports. If you need inference payloads retained immutably, that requires separate agreement due to storage costs — please indicate whether inference payloads are in-scope.

> Failover behavior (EU primary)
- Cross-region failover (EU->US) is supported under an agreed DR policy. Controls we offer during failover: automated notification to your security webhook, a maximum cross-region processing window (configurable, e.g., 72 hours), and optional automatic obfuscation of persisted PII fields while running in the non-primary region. If your policy disallows any cross-region processing, we can lock failover to within-region only.

> Data flow diagram / PII visibility
- See the attached draft map for an initial view of where PII touches systems and which caches are ephemeral. We will add explicit markers for any system that has access to cleartext and note redaction points.

Attachments and links:
- SOC2 Type II (latest): soc2-type2-redwood-2025.pdf (attached).
- Geo technical summary (sent earlier): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/medsource/geo-technical-summary
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4572

Proposed times for the tech call (30m):
- Thu 10:00 PT (09:00 MT / 12:00 ET)
- Fri 08:00 PT (07:00 MT / 10:00 ET)

If those don't work, send two times and we'll match. On the call we'll have Ben for architecture and Laura for compliance bindings; we'll capture action items to include in the MAP and return a redlined copy within 48 business hours.

Let me know which event classes you need retained immutably and whether inference payloads must be included. That will determine whether we need a separate storage/price annex in the contract.

Regards,
